question: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan and why is that month special?
note: p89: Ramadaan is the ninth month of the lunar calendar, in which the Qur'an was revealed; it contains Laylat-ul-Qadr.

resp.text: Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all past sins for whoever fasts its daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout the month. It is also distinguished with Laylat-ul-Qadr, a night that is better than a thousand months, during which spending time in prayer and remembering Allah brings forgiveness of all past sins. In addition, fasting during this month is the fourth pillar of Islam.

A ablução consiste em lavar o rosto, mãos e pés e passar a mão na cabeça de maneira específica. Ao realizá-la, você intenciona com o coração, diz em nome de ALLAH e lava as palmas das mãos começando pela direita. Em seguida, enxágua a boca e limpa o nariz inalando e retirando o ar. Então, esfrega a cabeça com as mãos molhadas, da frente até a nuca e trazendo de volta para a frente, e limpa as orelhas. Por fim, lava os pés até os tornozelos, começando pelo pé direito.

note: p104: animals that die without having been slaughtered are forbidden.

resp.text:
The meat of animals that die without having been slaughtered is forbidden. It is forbidden to eat animals that are not killed according to Islamic law. For slaughter, it is forbidden to use anything that kills the animal due to heavy weight or by hitting its head to death. In hunting wild animals, the name of Allah must be mentioned before discharging the weapon, and if the animal is found alive, it must be slaughtered.

question: Did the prophets really perform miracles? And what was Muhammad's miracle?
note: p31: Allah supported the messengers with miracles to prove their truthfulness; p38: those miracles ended with them, the Prophet's greatest miracle is the Qur'an, preserved after him.

resp.text: Yes, Allah supported the prophets with miracles to prove to people that they were true prophets. These miracles ended with the passing of those prophets. Allah also furnished Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with certain miracles to show his people and all mankind. The greatest miracle of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was Allah's Glorious Book, the Holy Qur'an. Allah took it upon Himself to preserve this book even after the demise of His Prophet ﷺ.

question: What's the 'Ibrahimi salawat' and where in the prayer do I say it?
note: p81: As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah ('O Allah, exalt Muhammad ... as You exalted Abraham ...') is recited after the tashahhud, and in the final sitting before the tasleem.

resp.text:
In prayers of three units like Maghrib or four units like Dhuhr, Asr, and Ishaa, you sit after completing the units to recite the first tashahhud and As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah. You recite it before concluding the prayer with the greetings of peace to the right and left.

question: Doesn't 'to you your religion and to me mine' mean every religion is equally valid?
note: p48: each side keeps to its own religion, the Prophet does not worship their false gods; p20/p22: Islam is the only religion Allah accepts (3:85).

resp.text: No, it does not mean that every religion is equally valid. Islam is the only true religion on the face of the earth. Allah has approved and chosen Islam for His servants and will not accept any other religion. With the final divine laws brought by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam. The verse means that you have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.
